¿Cómo se pasa de decimal a binario y a h: How do you convert from decimal to binary and hexadecimal?
Se divide entre 2 (o entre 16) y se leen: Divide by 2 (or by 16) and read the remainders backwards. 13 = 1101₂ (8 + 4 + 1) and 255 = FF₁₆.
¿Cómo se escribe un número negativo en c: How is a negative number written in two's complement and in BCD?
En complemento a 2 se invierten los bits: In two's complement, the bits of the positive number are inverted and 1 is added: with 8 bits, −5 is 11111011. In BCD each decimal digit takes 4 bits: 25 is 0010 0101.
En un sistema de base $b$ cada cifra pes: In a base-$b$ system each digit weighs a power of $b$ according to its position: $N = ∑ c_i · b^i$. Binary: $b = 2$ (digits 0 and 1). Hexadecimal: $b = 16$ (0-9 and A-F), so each digit equals 4 bits.
Con $n$ bits el primer bit pesa $−2^{n−1: With $n$ bits the first bit weighs $−2^{n−1}$ and the rest weigh positively, so the integers from $−2^{n−1}$ to $2^{n−1} − 1$ can be represented. To write a negative number: put its absolute value in $n$ bits, invert the bits and add 1 (equivalent to computing $2^n − |N|$). Addition and subtraction work just like with positives.
El BCD (decimal codificado en binario) e: BCD (binary-coded decimal) writes each decimal digit with 4 bits, from 0000 to 1001. It is not the same as converting the whole number to binary: 95 in BCD is 1001 0101, and in binary 0101 1111. It is used in clocks, calculators and seven-segment displays.
Una fracción se pasa a otra base multipl: A fraction is converted to another base by multiplying its fractional part by the base: the integer part is the digit and you continue with the remainder. If the remainder repeats, the expansion is periodic: $0.1 = 0.0\overline{0011}_2$, which is why 0.1 is not stored exactly on a binary machine. In IEEE 754 a number is $(−1)^s · 1.f · 2^{E − bias}$ with bias 127 (32 bits: 1 + 8 + 23) or 1023 (64 bits: 1 + 11 + 52). When adding in two's complement there is overflow if the carry into the sign bit differs from the carry out. Gray code changes only one bit from one number to the next.
